name: The Bund
address: 上海市黄浦区中山东一路
description: A riverside walk between Shanghai’s grand old facades and its future-facing skyline. Come back as the city lights up.
tip: The promenade can be crowded at sunset. Keep valuables close and use marked crossings.
hours: Outdoor promenade; access can change during events.
transit: East Nanjing Road station, Lines 2 / 10; walk to the river.

name: Yu Garden
address: 上海市黄浦区安仁街218号
description: Zigzag bridges, intricate rockeries, and quiet courtyards reveal a different rhythm in the heart of the old city.
tip: The ticketed garden and surrounding bazaar are separate. Check the official garden account for tickets and closures.
hours: Seasonal schedule and last admission: confirm with the official operator.
transit: Yuyuan Garden station, Lines 10 / 14; follow signs to the garden.

name: Wukang Road
address: 上海市徐汇区武康路（近淮海中路）
description: Plane-tree shade, Art Deco corners, and a coffee stop with no agenda. Walk slowly; the best discoveries are in between.
tip: This is a residential neighborhood. Avoid photographing inside homes and keep the pavement clear.
hours: Public street; individual cafés and shops keep their own hours.
transit: Shanghai Library station, Line 10; walk to Wukang Road.

name: Shanghai Museum East
address: 上海市浦东新区世纪大道1952号
description: Follow centuries of craftsmanship through bronzes, ceramics, and Chinese painting in a spacious contemporary museum.
tip: Bring your original passport. Interactive spaces need separate reservations; special exhibitions may charge.
hours: 10:00–18:00; last entry 17:00. Closed Tuesdays except national holidays. Recheck before visiting.
transit: Shanghai Science and Technology Museum station, Line 2; allow a walk.

name: Xintiandi
address: 上海市黄浦区太仓路181弄
description: Restored shikumen lanes meet an easy evening of restaurants, design shops, and people-watching.
tip: Restaurant prices vary widely. Check the menu before ordering; the lanes themselves do not need a ticket.
hours: Outdoor lanes; restaurant opening times vary.

name: Jing’an Temple
address: 上海市静安区南京西路1686号
description: Golden roofs rise above one of Shanghai’s busiest neighborhoods. Take a pause for the architecture and surrounding streets.
tip: An active place of worship. Dress respectfully, ask before taking photos, and verify admission at the entrance.
hours: Confirm current opening hours and ceremonial closures before visiting.

name: Nanjing Road
address: 上海市黄浦区南京东路步行街
description: A bright, busy slice of Shanghai, with department stores, old food shops, and an easy walk toward the waterfront.
tip: Decline unsolicited tea, art-show, and tour invitations. Confirm prices at established businesses.

name: Lujiazui Riverside
address: 上海市浦东新区滨江大道（陆家嘴段）
description: See the Bund from the other bank, beneath the towers that define modern Shanghai.
tip: This card covers the public riverside, not tower observation decks. Tower tickets are separate.
hours: Outdoor riverside; event access and ferry services vary.
transit: Lujiazui station, Lines 2 / 14; walk to Binjiang Avenue.

name: Fuxing Park
address: 上海市黄浦区雁荡路105号
description: A leafy pause for garden paths and a glimpse of everyday neighborhood life.
tip: Ask permission before photographing people. Park gates may close at night.
transit: South Shaanxi Road station, Lines 1 / 10 / 12; walk to the park.
